newsitem.title: UK: Nickel hits 2-yr low as stocks rise, outlook bleak.
newsitem.headline: Nickel hits 2-yr low as stocks rise, outlook bleak.

text.p: Nickel prices on Monday plunged to their lowest levels in two years against a background of rising stocks, while other key base metals showed a mixed trend.
Copper, the London Metals Exchange's (LME) flagship contract, rose to a five-month peak early in the day before profit-taking pared almost all the gains.
Traders said rising stocks and fund liquidation sent nickel plunging six percent to $6,620 a tonne, down $450 from Friday's finish. This is the lowest level since October 1994.
Subtantial tonnages of Russian nickel had arrived in Europe earlier this year and held off the LME in Rotterdam.
But as prices started to come down some traders decided to cut their losses by delivering the metal into LME warehouses, pushing up LME stocks in the process, traders said.
LME nickel inventories now stand at 44,508 tonnes, the highest since January.
An overhang of stainless steel scrap, an alternative source of nickel preferred by some steel mills, also weighed on values. Two thirds of the world's nickel is used in stainless steel.
Benchmark three month futures at one stage hit $6,600, but a late bout of buying emerged to lift prices slightly to $6,620, still well down on Friday's $7,050 close.
Some traders said further losses were likely in the short term, and first major support was pegged at $6,330.
Three-months copper moved in the opposite direction early in the day to a peak of $2,198, the highest level for five months.
Copper's earlier surge to near key resistance at $2,200 eased back under profit-taking and general liquidation. It closed at $2,159, up $11 from Friday.
Other base metals ended slightly weaker in sluggish trade.
In precious metals, gold sagged slightly towards key support, closing at $378.80/379.30, down 70 cents from Friday. Silver, platinum and palladium edged up from Friday's closes.
Soft commodities generally closed slightly weaker.
